slides.title: AI Use Cases in Healthcare Provider Operations

content_blocks.label: Subtitle
content_blocks.body: Research-backed executive example

content_blocks.label: Strapline
content_blocks.body: The strongest provider-operations AI use cases are workflow-embedded administrative domains where the system can cut manual coordination, reclaim clinician time, or accelerate revenue capture.

content_blocks.label: Why now
content_blocks.body: How healthcare AI adoption has shifted from pilots to operational deployment.

content_blocks.label: Where value is strongest
content_blocks.body: The workflows with the clearest near-term operational and financial proof.

content_blocks.label: Real examples
content_blocks.body: Documentation, access, revenue cycle, coding, and perioperative operations.

content_blocks.label: What to do
content_blocks.body: How a provider organization should prioritize pilots and governance.

slides.title: Healthcare AI Has Entered The Operational Phase
slides.objective: Create the first narrative turn in the deck.

content_blocks.label: Section note
content_blocks.body: The important question is no longer whether AI belongs in provider operations. It is which workflow should go first and how tightly it should be embedded into existing operating systems.

content_blocks.label: Operational AI is real now
content_blocks.body: Half of surveyed healthcare organizations report implemented gen AI and most have already shipped use cases.

content_blocks.label: Workflow fit matters more than generic capability
content_blocks.body: The best use cases are embedded in access, documentation, revenue cycle, coding, and capacity workflows.

content_blocks.label: Administrative domains are the cleanest first bets
content_blocks.body: They are repetitive, measurable, and less ambiguous than open-ended enterprise copilots.

content_blocks.label: Governance should follow workflow economics
content_blocks.body: Each pilot should have a domain owner, a baseline metric, and a clear operational scorecard.

slides.title: Highest-Value Provider-Ops AI Domains
slides.objective: Rank near-term operational value by workflow domain.

slides.title: What Tends To Win Versus What Tends To Stall
slides.objective: Differentiate high-fit workflows from vague AI ambitions.

content_blocks.label: What tends to win
content_blocks.body: EHR-embedded workflow steps|Clear operational owner|Direct cost, cash, or capacity metric|Repetitive high-volume tasks

content_blocks.label: What tends to stall
content_blocks.body: Generic enterprise copilots with unclear owners|No baseline metric for value|Workflows that are mostly governance theater|Point tools detached from daily operations

slides.title: Five High-Value Workflows
slides.objective: Translate the market evidence into a prioritized operating map.

content_blocks.label: Ambient documentation
content_blocks.body: Reduce note burden, improve patient interaction, and tighten downstream documentation quality.

content_blocks.label: Patient access + prior auth
content_blocks.body: Relieve queue pressure, reduce cancellations, and accelerate access to care.

content_blocks.label: Revenue cycle status work
content_blocks.body: Automate claim, auth, and document research to improve cash conversion.

content_blocks.label: Coding automation
content_blocks.body: Lower manual coding cost, reduce denials, and improve turnaround time.

content_blocks.label: Perioperative + capacity
content_blocks.body: Recover block time, improve scheduling precision, and grow cases without proportional staffing growth.

slides.title: Access and Authorization Is A Front-Door ROI Story
slides.objective: Show how one workflow family turns pain into measurable outcomes.

content_blocks.label: Queue pain
content_blocks.body: Fort HealthCare faced double the authorization work volume relative to staff capacity.

content_blocks.label: Call leakage
content_blocks.body: Thirty-eight percent of calls to a busy clinic were going to voicemail before automation.

content_blocks.label: Operational outcome
content_blocks.body: The system reached 91% successful authorizations, 74% digital completion, and over 5% fewer cancellations.

content_blocks.label: Implication 1
content_blocks.body: This is not just a convenience use case; it directly affects delayed care, cancellations, and staff overload.

content_blocks.label: Implication 2
content_blocks.body: Access workflows are strong pilot candidates because they have visible pain and clean operational baselines.

content_blocks.label: Implication 3
content_blocks.body: AI should be measured on queue relief and cancellation avoidance, not only chatbot activity.

slides.title: Revenue Cycle and Coding Create Hard-Dollar Proof
slides.objective: Show why finance-facing workflows are some of the easiest ROI cases to defend.

content_blocks.label: Revenue-cycle automation
content_blocks.body: AKASA highlights automated auth status, claim status, and research workflows inside RCM operations.

content_blocks.label: Cash and productivity outcomes
content_blocks.body: AKASA cites lower A/R days, staff time savings, gross yield improvement, and better efficiency.

content_blocks.label: Coding proof
content_blocks.body: CodaMetrix cites lower coding cost, faster turnaround, lower denials, and 5:1 ROI economics.

content_blocks.label: Implication 1
content_blocks.body: Finance leaders can govern these pilots against cost-to-collect, A/R days, denial rates, and coding productivity.

content_blocks.label: Implication 2
content_blocks.body: These are enterprise workflows, but they still need narrow initial boundaries to avoid overpromising.

content_blocks.label: Implication 3
content_blocks.body: A good provider strategy treats revenue cycle and coding as operational AI lanes, not just back-office IT projects.

slides.title: Documentation and Capacity Use Cases Show Different Kinds of Value
slides.objective: Contrast clinician-time value with throughput and access value.

content_blocks.label: Clinician workflow value
content_blocks.body: UCHealth scaled Abridge after a pilot and uses ambient documentation to reduce administrative burden and improve patient interaction.

content_blocks.label: Capacity value
content_blocks.body: Saint Luke's handled 7% more surgical cases despite 20% fewer ORs by improving perioperative scheduling efficiency.

content_blocks.label: Management lesson
content_blocks.body: One class of use case reclaims clinician time; another unlocks constrained system capacity.

content_blocks.label: Implication 1
content_blocks.body: Documentation tools should be judged on clinician experience and downstream documentation quality, not just raw note speed.

content_blocks.label: Implication 2
content_blocks.body: Capacity tools should be judged on throughput, access, and staff-load efficiency.

content_blocks.label: Implication 3
content_blocks.body: A provider AI roadmap should not force every use case into the same ROI frame.

slides.title: How A Health System Should Prioritize

content_blocks.body: Pick one workflow family|Choose a high-pain domain such as prior auth, coding, or OR scheduling instead of a vague enterprise AI mandate.
Define the scorecard|Tie the pilot to one operational owner and 2-3 metrics like cancellations, A/R days, denials, or clinician time.
Embed in workflow|Require EHR integration and downstream process ownership before declaring the use case viable.
Separate assistive from autonomous|Documentation, coding support, and contact-center workflows have different governance and safety profiles.
Scale only after proof|Expand once a workflow has measurable, durable operational gains rather than vendor-driven narrative momentum.

content_blocks.label: This is a research-backed synthesis
content_blocks.body: The deck uses current market research plus official company and customer-story evidence, not one normalized benchmark dataset.

content_blocks.label: The evidence is stronger for workflow categories than for vendor ranking
content_blocks.body: The purpose is to identify which operational domains are strongest, not to declare one vendor a universal winner.

content_blocks.label: Use this for prioritization, not procurement
content_blocks.body: Any production decision still needs local baseline metrics, workflow mapping, compliance review, and total-cost-of-change analysis.

content_blocks.label: Main message
content_blocks.body: Start where the workflow is repetitive, measurable, and operationally owned; scale only after hard proof.
